page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-800s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor. The system is configured with 4 shared vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 800 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server type.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing the instance in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores align with the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth write tests for large blocks and single-threaded gzip compression both achieve strong ratings in the top 25%. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are weaker, falling into the bottom 25% tier. LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are average, but drop to poor or weak tiers when executing a medium 7B model.

The instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources. Because the CPU allocation is shared, workloads requiring sustained, predictable multi-core processing may experience performance variability. The combination of 32.0 GB of RAM and 800 GB of NVMe SSD storage makes this server type suitable for memory-optimized applications, caching layers, and general-purpose workloads.
